To Timothy my dearly beloved son
pax a Deo Patre et Christo Iesu Domino n: and peace, from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Lord
quod sine intermissione habeam tui memor: that without ceasing, I have a remembrance of thee in my prayers, night and day
Recordationem accipiens eius fidei que e: Calling to mind that faith which is in thee unfeigned
Que et habitavit primum in avia tua: which also dwelt first in thy grandmother
Loide et matre tua Eunice, certus sum au: Lois, and in thy mother Eunice, and I am certain
admoneo te, ut resuscites gratiam Dei: I admonish thee, that thou stir up the grace of God
sed virtutis et dilectionis et sobrietat: but of power, and of love, and of sobriety
testimonium Domini nostri,: of the testimony of our Lord
secundum virtutem Dei: according to the power of God
non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum: not according to our works, but according to his own purpose
et gratiam que data est nobis in Christo: and grace which was given us in Christ Jesus
autem nunc per illuminationem salvatoris: But is now made manifest by the illumination of our Saviour
etiam hec: For which cause I also suffer these things
et certus sum, quia potens est depositum: and I am certain that he is able to keep that which I have committed
QUIA POTENS EST DEPOSITUM MEUM SERVARE: For he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him, against that day
Formam habens sanorum verborum: Hold the form of sound words
que a me: which thou hast heard of me
audisti in fide et dilectione: hast heard of me in faith, and in the love
bonum depositum: the good thing committed to thy trust
per Spiritum sanctum qui habitat in nobi: by the Holy Ghost, who dwelleth in us
Scis hoc quod aversi sunt a me omnes qui: Thou knowest this, that all they who are in Asia are turned away from me
of whom are Phigellus and Hermogenes
Det misericordiam Dominus Honesifori: The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus
quia sepe me refrigeravit: because he hath often refreshed me
sed cum Romam venisset, sollicite me que: But when he was come to Rome, he carefully sought me
invenire misericordiam a Domino: to find mercy of the Lord
Et quanta Ephesi: And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus
fili mi, confortare in gratia: my son, be strong in the grace
Et que audisti a me: And the things which thou hast heard of me
hec commenda fidelibus: the same commend to faithful men
hominibus qui idonei: who shall be fit to teach others also
sicut bonus miles in Christo Iesu: as a good soldier of Christ Jesus
that he may please him to whom he hath engaged himself
Nam et qui certat in agone: For he also that striveth for the mastery
NAM ET QUI CERTAT: For he also that striveth for the mastery
agricolam oportet primum de fructibus pe: must first partake of the fruits
enim tibi Dominus in omnibus: for the Lord will give thee in all things understanding
Dominum Iesum Christum resurrexisse a mo: that the Lord Jesus Christ is risen again from the dead, of the seed of David
usque ad vincula quasi: even unto bands, as an evildoer
the word of God is not bound
sustineo propter electos,: I endure for the sake of the elect
ut et ipsi salutem: that they also may obtain the salvation
sermo. Nam si commortui sumus,: saying: for if we be dead with him
et convivemus;: we shall live also with him
et conregnabimus;: we shall also reign with him
Hec commone,: Of these things put them in mind
HEC COMMONE: Of these things put them in mind
Noli verbis contendere. Ad nihil enim ut: Contend not in words, for it is to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.
inconfusibilem,: that needeth not to be ashamed
rightly handling the word of truth
eorum ut cancer serpit. Ex quibus: spreadeth like a canker: of whom
qui a veritate: Who have erred from the truth
have subverted the faith of some
non solum sunt vasa aurea et argentea,: there are not only vessels of gold and silver
sed et lignea et fictilia,: but also of wood and earth
VASA AUREA ET ARGENTEA ET LIGNEA: vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood
call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
questiones devita, sciens quia generant: questions, knowing that they beget strifes.
Servum autem Domini non oportet litigare: But the servant of the Lord must not wrangle,
eos qui resistunt veritati. Nequando: them that resist the truth. Lest at any time
NEQUANDO DET DEUS ILLIS PENITENTIAM: lest at any time God give them repentance
et resipiscant a diaboli laqueis,: And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil,
homines se ipsos amantes,: Men shall be lovers of themselves,
Ex his enim sunt: For of these sort are they
who are led away with divers desires
Semper discentes et numquam ad scientiam: Ever learning, and never attaining to the knowledge of the truth
resistunt veritati, homines corrupti men: resist the truth, men corrupted in mind
ultra non proficient. Insipientia: shall proceed no farther; for their folly
enim eorum manifesta erit omnibus,: for their folly shall be manifest to all men
mihi facta sunt Antiochie Iconii Lystris: came upon me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra
and out of them all the Lord delivered me
in his que didicisti,: in those things which thou hast learned
quia ab infantia sacras litteras: because from thy infancy thou hast known the holy scriptures
te possunt instruere ad salutem per fide: which can instruct thee to salvation, by the faith
ut perfectus sit: That the man of God may be perfect
coram Deo et Christo Iesu qui iudicaturu: before God and Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead
Erit enim tempus: For there shall be a time
cum sanam doctrinam non sustinebunt,: when they will not endure sound doctrine
sed ad sua desideria: but, according to their own desires
coacervabunt sibi magistros: they will heap to themselves teachers
et a veritate: And will indeed turn away their hearing from the truth
quidem auditum avertent, ad fabulas aute: but will be turned unto fables
labora, opus fac evangeliste,: labour, do the work of an evangelist
OPUS FAC EVANGELISTE: Do the work of an evangelist
iam delibor,: am even now ready to be sacrificed
et tempus mee resolutionis: and the time of my dissolution
Bonum certamen certavi,: I have fought a good fight
I have finished, I have kept the faith
reposita est mihi corona iustitie,: there is laid up for me a crown of justice
quam reddet mihi Dominus in illa die: which the Lord will render to me in that day
iustus iudex. Non solum autem mihi, sed: the just judge. And not only to me, but to them also that love his coming
Festina venire ad me cito: Make haste to come to me quickly
diligens hoc seculum, et abiit Thessalon: loving this world, and is gone to Thessalonica, Crescens
Penulam autem quam reliqui Troade: The cloak that I left at Troas
veniens affer tecum et libros, maxime au: when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, especially the parchments
sed omnes me dereliquerunt. Non illis re: but all forsook me: may it not be laid to their charge
NON ILLI REPUTETUR: may it not be laid to their charge
Dominus autem mihi astitit: But the Lord stood by me
et confortavit me, ut per me predicatio: and strengthened me, that by me the preaching may be accomplished, and that all the Gentiles may hear: and I was delivered
out of the mouth of the lion
DE ORE LEONIS: out of the mouth of the lion
ab omni opere malo et salvum faciet: from every evil work and will preserve me
festina ante hiemem venire: Make haste to come before winter
